historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue (10-year CAGR 2.2%, FY26/27 guidance of space +1% plus low-single-digit LFL), not equity
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1.3% to -2.6%) and statutory EPS CAGR (-13% to -16%) diverge by far more than 30% from revenue. Both are distorted: equity shrinks because GBP 1.9bn of buybacks and dividends since FY2021 exceed earnings, and statutory EPS carries GBP 150-400m/yr of goodwill, store and JV impairments (FY2020, FY2023, FY2025, FY2026). Adjusted EPS rose 14.9% to 23.8p in FY25/26 and 16% in H1 FY26/27, almost entirely from the shrinking share count. Growth is therefore selected from revenue and guidance; book-value compounding is the wrong lens for a buyback-funded retailer.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (treatment B: CSV FCF less lease principal and interest from FY2020 when IFRS 16 began, less SBC, less interest income), GBP m: FY2016 461, FY2017 347, FY2018 -99, FY2019 282, FY2020 42, FY2021 873, FY2022 267, FY2023 -118, FY2024 434, FY2025 423, FY2026 488. The 3-year CAGR is undefined (FY2023 negative after a GBP 300m+ working-capital build); the 5-year CAGR runs from the COVID peak and is meaningless as a trend; FY2019 to FY2026 (both pre- and post-IFRS-16 figures carry the lease cost) gives 8.1%, flattered by the FY2026 one-off tax receipt. SBC is 0.15-0.21% of revenue throughout, so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs barely differ; the swing factor in this series is working capital, not compensation.

scenario_narratives.base: Kingfisher remains a low-growth, cash-generative European DIY retailer. The UK (52% of sales) grinds forward on Screwfix expansion, TradePoint and Homebase share gains while B&Q big-ticket stays soft; France (30%) stabilises but only partially closes the margin gap to the 5-7% target because the market recovery is outside management's control; Poland and Iberia add a point of group growth. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin edges from 10.4% to 11.0% by FY2032, lease intensity drifts down slightly, capex runs at the guided 3% of sales, cash tax normalises to 26% after the FY25/26 HMRC windfall. Owner FCF starts around GBP 330m (excluding working-capital releases and interest income) and compounds with the margin to roughly GBP 470m by year 10; most of the headline 'GBP 500m+ FCF' is distributed, not reinvested, so the share count keeps shrinking but that is value-neutral here.
scenario_narratives.bull: The French DIY market, down ~10% since 2024, turns in 2027 and the already half-completed Castorama store programme lets management hit the 5-7% France retail margin by FY2031. Screwfix keeps its 14-quarter growth streak, the City format opens the runway to 1,000+ UK stores, trade sales reach GBP 5bn and marketplace plus retail media lift gross margin. Group pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 12%, French rightsizing cuts lease cash to 3.5% of sales, growth runs 3-3.5% for four years and terminal growth is 2.5%. This is the RBC/Outperform world and it needs two independent things to go right: the French consumer and UK execution.
scenario_narratives.bear: A rates-driven consumer squeeze hits UK and French housing activity in FY27/28, big-ticket kitchens and bathrooms (14-15% of sales) fall double digits and LFL goes negative for two years. Leroy Merlin presses its French scale advantage, the Castorama turnaround stalls at 2-3% margins, and UK competitive pricing plus employer NI and wage inflation compress the group margin to 9.5% (where it sat in FY2019-20). Rent inflation on a flat top line lifts lease cash to 4% of sales. Impairments recur but the balance sheet (net cash ex-leases, BBB) holds; the damage is to the earnings base, not solvency. This is the JPMorgan/Deutsche Sell-case world.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Kingfisher as a stream of owner free cash flow after the real cost of its stores: IFRS 16 lease cash (GBP ~500m a year, 3.8% of sales) is charged through the flows and lease liabilities are kept out of the bridge, SBC (small, 0.2% of sales) is expensed and the share count held flat, interest income is stripped because the net cash it earns is added in the bridge, and cash tax is normalised to the 26% guided rate rather than the FY25/26 windfall-depressed GBP 65m. The forward margin is built from components anchored on the FY2024-26 run-rate and the raised FY26/27 guidance, not on the COVID-era FY2021-22 peak or the impairment-laden FY2020 trough. Three scenarios turn on the two axes that actually decide the stock: whether France recovers toward the 5-7% margin target, and whether the UK consumer and Screwfix hold up. Discounted at a GBP WACC of 9% with a 14x terminal cap, and no second risk premium stacked on top of the scenario weights.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lease treatment: charging GBP ~500m of lease cash through the flows is the single largest adjustment; a reader comparing against the company's GBP 500m+ FCF or EV/EBITDA on post-IFRS-16 EBITDA (1,321m) must use lease-consistent multiples (ex-lease EV vs EBITDA less lease cash, ~GBP 824m)

Working capital: the component build assumes zero structural release; FY2024-26 benefited from GBP 80-100m/yr inventory reductions and the company's FY26/27 FCF guidance embeds more. If releases persist for several years, the base is ~GBP 50m/yr (3p/share/yr) too conservative; if inventory rebuilds, reported FCF will undershoot guidance
France (30% of sales) margin path: each 1pp of France retail margin is ~GBP 40m EBITDA, ~0.3pp group margin, roughly 25-30p/share at the base multiple
Cyclicality and weather: big-ticket (14-15% of sales) and seasonal categories swing with rates, housing and summer weather; the bear case is a repeat of FY2019-20 margins, not a tail event
FX translation: ~45% of sales in EUR/PLN; a 5% GBP move shifts reported revenue by ~GBP 300m and EBITDA by ~GBP 25-30m without any operating change

Terminal value and discount rate: with a 9% WACC and 14x cap the terminal is roughly half of enterprise value; the sensitivity grid and required-return table show how quickly 318p becomes a 10-11% IRR rather than a bargain

Impairments and adjusting items (GBP 150-400m/yr statutory in four of the last seven years) are mostly non-cash and excluded here; the cash element of restructuring (store exits, Romania) is inside OCF and therefore inside the EBITDA margin anchor

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/KGF.L) at inputs.price_as_of; GBp quote; 52-week range 266.4-372.3
data_sources.financials: research/KGF.L/Reports/KGF.L_Metrics.csv (GBP millions, FY2016-FY2026 annual plus half-years) and kpis table; FY2025/26 Annual Report (KGF.L_Annual_FY2026.txt: cash flow statement line ~8690, share capital note 11521, leases note 10530-10566, net debt/EBITDA table 2222, EPS note 10190); H1 FY26/27 results to 31 July 2026 (KGF.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt: guidance lines 99-108, net debt note 16 line 1670, share capital note 13 line 1596, EPS note line 1454, cash flow statement line 1111)
data_sources.qualitative: research/KGF.L/Reports/KGF.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, France margin target, trade/e-commerce ambitions, bull/bear cases, sell-side range 245-375p

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 31 July 2026: 1,650m shares in issue (H1 FY26/27 note 13) less c.3m held by the ESOP trust plus 30m dilutive potential ordinary shares (H1 FY26/27 EPS note: basic WA 1,677m, diluted 1,707m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count would charge it twice. The company is a heavy repurchaser (88m shares cancelled in FY25/26, 61m in H1 FY26/27, 2m more post balance sheet), so the flat count is funded many times over; buybacks are value-neutral in this model and the cash they consume is what the DCF is valuing.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net CASH of GBP 309m at 31 July 2026, EXCLUDING lease liabilities (treatment B below). Cash 312 + short-term deposits 100 = 412; debt = fixed-term loans 99 + bank loans 1 + overdrafts 2 + net financing derivatives 1 = 103 (H1 FY26/27 note 16). The company's own 'net debt' of GBP 1,931m includes GBP 2,240m of IFRS 16 lease liabilities, which this model charges through the flows instead. Net UK pension surplus (GBP 181m) less overseas deficit (GBP 98m) is left out of the bridge: the UK surplus is not readily accessible. Koctaş Turkey JV carried at nil.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025/26 (year to 31 Jan 2026): OCF 1,433 - capex 388 (PPE 303 + intangibles 85) = 1,045 (the Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow), less lease principal 379 and lease interest 118 = 548. Company-defined free cash flow was GBP 512m (also after net interest and other items). FY25/26 flattered by a GBP 64m one-off HMRC receipt (EU CFC state-aid annulment) and cash tax paid of only GBP 65m against a GBP 133m charge; a normalised owner FCF for FY25/26 is roughly GBP 360-420m. The forward path is built from components, not carried from this figure.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025/26 Annual Report, consolidated cash flow note 32 and note 31 Share-based payments: share-based compensation charge GBP 27m (FY24/25: GBP 20m). No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed (ESOP trust purchases of GBP 25m are the settlement mechanism and are counted in buyback_cash); EquityAwardTaxes recorded as 0 in the CSV. Note: Kingfisher's adjusted EBITDA (GBP 1,321m) is already AFTER the SBC charge, so ebitda_margin_path below is stated PRE-SBC (1,348/12,945 = 10.41%) and the engine's SBC deduction brings it back to the reported figure.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income GBP 33m FY25/26 (interest received GBP 31m). Stripped from the FCF base because the cash that earns it sits in the equity bridge as net cash (matching-asset rule). Net cash is below 1x the FCF base, but leaving the income in while adding the cash would still count it twice.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025/26 financing outflow: GBP 256m purchase of own shares for cancellation + GBP 25m for the ESOP trust. H1 FY26/27: GBP 189m + GBP 27m. A GBP 300m programme (5th tranche series) started March 2026; GBP 125m completed by September, GBP 50m third tranche running to December 2026. Dividends GBP 218m FY25/26 on top.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model per-share values in GBP to the GBp quote basis; no market FX is involved, so the rate does not go stale. No dual listing to parity-check. Operating exposure: ~45% of sales earned in EUR/PLN and translated into GBP; FY26/27 guidance assumes current exchange rates (GBP/EUR ~1.18 at 2026-10-09, Yahoo GBPEUR=X).
inputs.fy0_note: FY2026 = Kingfisher's fiscal year 2025/26, ended 31 January 2026. Y1 of the projection is FY2027 (2026/27), for which guidance exists.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:49:17Z (LSE regular session close, 9 Oct 2026; Yahoo chart API, currency GBp, 52-week range 266.4-372.3)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows: UK 10-year gilt ~4.5%, equity risk premium ~5.0%, levered beta ~1.0-1.1 for a cyclical European big-box retailer gives a cost of equity ~9.5-10%; financial debt is negligible once leases are treated as an operating cost (treatment B), so WACC ~9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, French market risk and weather are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the discount rate. Terminal cap 14x FCF (the method's 12-15x band for a cyclical, structurally slow-growth business; Gordon at 9%/2% would be 14.6x).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full IFRS 16 cash lease payment (FY25/26 principal GBP 379m + interest GBP 118m = GBP 497m, 3.84% of sales; FY24/25 GBP 510m, 3.99%) is deducted inside owner EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (GBP 2,240m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Cash-tax EBIT therefore uses D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: FY25/26 total D&A 667 less ROU depreciation 324 (leases note) = 343, 2.65% of sales (FY24/25: 656 - 325 = 331, 2.59%). Sanity multiples must be lease-consistent: ex-lease EV against EBITDA less lease cash (~GBP 824m), not against post-IFRS-16 adjusted EBITDA of GBP 1,321m.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; profit attributable to equity shareholders equals group profit. Koctaş (Turkey, 50%) is an equity-accounted JV written down to nil in FY25/26 and contributes nothing to the flows or the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, probability-weighted, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer' with the owner-fcf-adaptations (GBP WACC, single lease treatment B, SBC-light market, pence quote). Kingfisher is a pure operating retailer (B&Q, Screwfix, Castorama, Brico Depot) with freehold property used in the business, so no sum-of-parts. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. OUTLIERS: FY2020 net income GBP 8m (IFRS 16 transition year plus GBP ~400m of impairments, Russia/Iberia exits) and FY2021-22 (COVID DIY boom: FCF GBP 1,369m/843m net income, LFL +7-10%) are treated as outliers, not trend; the base anchors on the FY2024-26 run-rate and FY26/27 guidance. GUIDANCE (22 Sep 2026, raised): adjusted PBT GBP 595-635m (FY25/26 560), free cash flow GBP 480-520m, capex c.GBP 400m, net finance costs c.GBP 105m, adjusted ETR c.26%, space +1%. Guidance FCF includes a working-capital inflow and interest income and is before SBC; the component build here excludes the working-capital release (wc_capture 0) because inventory reduction is a programme, not a perpetuity. 10-year horizon because the France margin recovery (2.5-3.6% retail margin today vs 5-7% medium-term target on 30% of sales) is still ramping at year 5 in the base and bull cases.

bear.rationale: A UK/French consumer downturn in FY27/28 (higher-for-longer rates, weak housing transactions, elevated French savings) takes LFL negative for two years; France stays a distant number two to Leroy Merlin with margins stuck at 2-3%; Wickes/Toolstation price competition and UK NI/wage inflation compress the group pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 9.5% (FY2019-20 territory, ~9.1-9.6%); rent inflation lifts lease cash to 4.0% of sales on a shrinking top line. No solvency issue: net cash ex-leases, BBB, undrawn GBP 650m RCF. Bear terminal FCF stays well above the zero floor.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 1.5%: H1 FY26/27 sales +0.8% reported with FX tailwind, space +1% guided, B&Q LFL -2.9% on heatwaves vs Screwfix +5.6%. Y2-5 2.5%: Screwfix roll-out (City format), trade to GBP 5bn, e-commerce to 30%, Poland/Iberia growth, against flat-to-declining mature UK/France DIY markets. Fades to 2.0% nominal (roughly inflation) by Y7. 10-year revenue CAGR 2.2% matches the FY2016-26 actual.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin FY25/26 10.41% (FY24/25 10.25%). Guidance midpoint (adj PBT 615 + finance costs 105 + D&A ~680) implies ~10.6% in FY26/27 including a GBP 14m one-off business-rates refund, so Y1 10.55%. Ramps 45bp to 11.0% by Y6: about one-third of the France 5-7% retail margin target delivered (France is 30% of sales; full delivery would add ~0.9pp at group level), plus OEB/retail-media mix, net of UK wage and NI inflation. Flat thereafter.
base.lease_rationale: Lease cash 3.84% of sales FY25/26, 3.99% FY24/25, 3.65% FY23/24. Base drifts from 3.85% to 3.75% as Castorama rightsizing and franchise conversions trim the French estate while Screwfix compact stores add low-rent space.
base.capex_tax_rationale: Capex c.3% of sales per guidance (FY26/27 c.GBP 400m). Owned-asset D&A 2.65% (667 total less 324 ROU). Cash tax 26% on pre-IFRS-16 EBIT, the guided adjusted ETR; FY25/26 cash tax of GBP 65m was abnormally low and is not carried forward. Working capital capture 0: inventory and payables roughly offset for a big-box retailer, and the GBP 80-100m/yr releases of recent years are a programme, not a perpetuity.

bull.rationale: French DIY market stabilises from 2027 and the Castorama transformation delivers the 5-7% retail margin target by Y5-6 (worth ~0.9pp at group level); Screwfix compounds toward 1,000+ UK stores; trade reaches GBP 5bn and marketplace/retail media lift mix. Group pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 12.0%, lease intensity falls to 3.5% on French rightsizing, and nominal growth runs 3-3.5% for four years. Cash tax 25.5% on a slightly higher Poland/Iberia mix.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull weight cut to 25% because the bull case requires two independent events, a French market recovery that management itself says is outside its control and sustained UK share gains in a competitive trade market. Bear weight raised to 25% because this is a cyclical consumer-discretionary retailer whose margins compressed to this degree as recently as FY2019-20 without any recession, and because H1 FY26/27 already showed B&Q LFL -2.9%; it is not raised further because there is no going-concern, covenant or refinancing risk (net cash ex-leases, BBB stable, undrawn RCF). Base at 50% sits on raised FY26/27 guidance and a consensus Hold.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
